about: The variables of when conditions, which are CEL expressions, and examples the Go and the TypeScript evaluators are both tested against. Only the Go reader of the manifest checks types, so the TypeScript tests leave out the invalid conditions that are type errors. `target` is what the command runs over, as its place gives it; `version` is a text version of the file, set only where a command lists one item per version; `window` is the window the command is offered in; `config` holds every setting by its dotted key.

variables.name: target.isRoot
variables.about: the target is the root folder of the vault

variables.name: target.isMultiple
variables.about: the target is one of several paths selected together

variables.name: target.isFile
variables.about: the target is a file that is not a note

variables.name: target.contentType
variables.about: the content type of the target, such as application/pdf; empty for a folder

variables.name: target.noteType
variables.about: the type of the note, such as link; empty where the target is no note

variables.name: target.properties
variables.about: the frontmatter of the note by its keys, as target.properties.media; empty where the target is no note

variables.name: version.kind
variables.about: the kind of the text version, as the plugin that made it names it

variables.name: version.isLive
variables.about: the text version is the one shown and indexed now

variables.name: window.isVaultOpen
variables.about: a vault is open in the window

variables.name: window.isVaultReady
variables.about: the vault of the window is open and read

variables.name: config
variables.about: every setting by its dotted key, as config.editor.lineNumbers

invalid.about: a variable that is not declared
a string compared with a number
an expression that is not a condition
